subject.title: [Bug]: web_fetch reports exact-size responses as truncated

question: Should `readResponseText` treat exact-limit streamed bodies as complete by adopting an explicit overread/content-length contract, or should cap-equals-truncated remain the current behavior until a real failing response proves otherwise?
rationale: Current source supports the reporter's boundary claim, but a member already rejected the same standalone inference tweak without a concrete contract or real failing response, and the open candidate PR changes bounded stream waiting behavior.

options.title: Require contract or real proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical report and require the open candidate PR to define and prove the overread/content-length contract before landing.

options.title: Accept the overread fix now
options.body: Treat exact-limit non-truncation as the intended helper contract and land a repaired candidate PR with empty-chunk-safe lookahead and focused tests.

options.title: Close as intentional cap behavior
options.body: Decide that reaching the byte cap is intentionally reported as truncated unless a future real response proves a user-facing failure.

recommendation.title: Require contract or real proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical report and require the open candidate PR to define and prove the overread/content-length contract before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: He made the prior same-cluster maintainer decision and is tied to the current helper history.
